Reproducing Zandvakili and Kohn (2015) on CRCNS v1v2-1¶

Paper: A. Zandvakili and A. Kohn, "Coordinated Neuronal Activity Enhances Corticocortical Communication", Neuron 87, 827-839 (2015), doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2015.07.026.

Dataset: CRCNS v1v2-1, "Simultaneous V1-V2 neuronal population recordings in anesthetized macaque monkeys" (Zandvakili and Kohn 2019), doi:10.6080/K0B27SHN, read from the public S3 bucket crcnsarchive at v1v2-1/live/v1-v2_gratings.zip, opened in place.

Version: CRCNS data sets are not versioned, so the version is recorded as unversioned (docs/archives.md, CRCNS). The bucket holds one copy of the data, under live/ (uploaded 2026-02-11), with data description version 0.5 (Feb 15, 2019); there is no other version to choose, and the paper cites none. The files read are pinned by the MD5 sums of the data set's checksums.md5: v1-v2_gratings.zip 12a15c5a63366ccd1fa2b4e495f1d66d, docs/crcns_v1v2-1_data_description.pdf 72e436e8e0c006efbbe5eab4737c3c69, docs/sessions_description.pdf 48917aea682f869c7aee45f170516c7d. The first cell below checks the listed sum of the zip against these.

Claims: claims/zandvakili-2015.yaml, written from the version of record with its supplement. The data set holds 5 sessions from 3 animals of the paper's 7; the paper's counts describe the larger sample, so fractions, medians and comparisons are what is tested.

Shared methods are in the helper v1v2.py, whose docstring says where each parameter comes from. Random seeds are fixed; each claim's section draws from its own generator.

Load and compute¶

Each session is loaded, its CCGs computed for all pairs of kept units (both jitter windows), and the V1 state histograms around every V2 spike computed (helper session_ccgs, session_divergence). The session's spikes are then released, so that one session is in memory at a time. This is the long cell (several minutes).

In [2]:
L = 2 * h.MAXLAG + 1
LAGS = np.arange(-h.MAXLAG, h.MAXLAG + 1)
pairs, sites, sess_info, div, sig_ccgs, clock, dup = [], [], {}, {}, [], [], []

def decode_acc(X, y, rng):
    """Nearest class mean on z-scored counts, two-fold cross-validation (a standard choice)."""
    X = (X - X.mean(0)) / (X.std(0) + 1e-9)
    idx = rng.permutation(len(y)); half = np.zeros(len(y), bool); half[idx[: len(y) // 2]] = True
    acc = []
    for tr in (half, ~half):
        cls = np.unique(y)
        mu = np.stack([X[tr & (y == c)].mean(0) for c in cls])
        d = ((X[~tr][:, None, :] - mu[None]) ** 2).sum(-1)
        acc.append(np.mean(cls[d.argmin(1)] == y[~tr]))
    return float(np.mean(acc))

for si, name in enumerate(h.SESSIONS):
    t = time.time()
    s = h.load_session(z, name)
    k1, k2 = h.keep_units(s, "V1"), h.keep_units(s, "V2")
    n_tr = len(s["stim"])
    sess_info[name] = dict(animal=name[:3], n_rows=s["n_rows"], n_driven=n_tr,
                           stim_counts=np.bincount(s["stim"])[1:].tolist(),
                           v1_units=s["V1"]["n_units"], v2_units=s["V2"]["n_units"],
                           v1_kept=len(k1), v2_kept=len(k2),
                           v1_rate=s["V1"]["rate"], v2_rate=s["V2"]["rate"],
                           v1_codes=s["V1"]["codes"], v2_codes=s["V2"]["codes"],
                           v1_rf=s["V1"]["rf"], v2_rf=s["V2"]["rf"], fields=s["fields"],
                           trial_id_increasing=bool(np.all(np.diff(s["trial_id"]) > 0)),
                           row_alternates=bool(np.all(s["row_stim"][1::2] == 0) and np.all(s["row_stim"][0::2] > 0)))
    # clock check: decode orientation from V1 counts in windows around stimulus onset
    rng = np.random.default_rng(100 + si)
    u, tr, tt = s["V1"]["events"]; m = np.isin(u, k1)
    bu, btr, btt = s["V1"]["blank_events"]; bm = np.isin(bu, k1)
    umap = np.full(u.max() + 1, -1); umap[k1] = np.arange(len(k1))
    for lo, hi, label in [(-100, 0, "last 100 ms of preceding blank"), (0, 30, "0-30 ms"), (30, 60, "30-60 ms"),
                          (60, 160, "60-160 ms"), (1180, 1280, "1180-1280 ms")]:
        X = np.zeros((n_tr, len(k1)))
        if lo < 0:
            # blank row k precedes driven trial k + 1 (rows alternate driven, blank)
            mm = bm & (btt >= 1500 + lo) & (btr < n_tr - 1)
            np.add.at(X, (btr[mm] + 1, umap[bu[mm]]), 1)
            keep = np.arange(1, n_tr)
        else:
            mm = m & (tt >= lo) & (tt < hi)
            np.add.at(X, (tr[mm], umap[u[mm]]), 1)
            keep = np.arange(n_tr)
        acc = decode_acc(X[keep], s["stim"][keep], rng)
        # shifted labels: the same counts against the next trial's stimulus
        acc_shift = decode_acc(X[keep][:-1], s["stim"][keep][1:], rng)
        clock.append(dict(session=name, window=label, accuracy=acc, shifted_labels=acc_shift))
    # population PSTH onset (all orientations), for the latency check
    psth = np.bincount(tt[m], minlength=h.T_MS) / (n_tr * len(k1)) * 1000
    sess_info[name]["psth"] = psth
    # mean V1 population response per stimulus, 50-1280 ms, for the orientation check
    resp = np.zeros((8, len(k1)))
    mm = m & (tt >= 50)
    np.add.at(resp, (s["stim"][tr[mm]] - 1, umap[u[mm]]), 1)
    sess_info[name]["resp"] = resp / (np.bincount(s["stim"])[1:, None])

    cc = h.session_ccgs(s)
    units = cc["units"]
    area = np.array([a for a, _ in units]); uidx = np.array([i for _, i in units])
    elec = np.array([s[a]["codes"][i, 0] for a, i in units])
    nsp = cc["n_spikes"]
    iu, ju = np.triu_indices(len(units), 1)
    q = (h.T_MS - np.abs(LAGS)) / h.T_MS
    norm = q[None, :] * nsp[iu][:, None]
    raw = cc["raw"][iu, ju] / norm
    sc = (cc["raw"][iu, ju] - cc["shuffle"][iu, ju]) / norm
    jc = {w: (cc["raw"][iu, ju] - cc["jitter"][w][iu, ju]) / norm for w in cc["jitter"]}
    # duplicate check: fraction of the sparser unit's spikes coincident at lag 0
    zero_frac = cc["raw"][iu, ju, h.MAXLAG] / np.minimum(nsp[iu], nsp[ju])
    for k in np.where(zero_frac > 0.5)[0]:
        dup.append(dict(session=name, a=units[iu[k]], b=units[ju[k]], frac=zero_frac[k]))
    del cc
    ptype = np.char.add(area[iu], area[ju])
    df = pd.DataFrame(dict(session=name, animal=name[:3], type=ptype, i=uidx[iu], j=uidx[ju],
                           elec_i=elec[iu], elec_j=elec[ju], n_i=nsp[iu], n_j=nsp[ju],
                           zero_frac=zero_frac))
    for w in jc:
        sm = h.gauss_smooth(jc[w])
        sig, peak, lag, sd = h.significance(sm)
        df[f"sig{w}"] = sig; df[f"peak{w}"] = peak; df[f"lag{w}"] = lag; df[f"sd{w}"] = sd
        if w == 10:
            ks = np.where(sig)[0]
            li = lag[ks] + h.MAXLAG
            df.loc[ks, "width_s"] = [h.half_width(sm[k], l) for k, l in zip(ks, li)]
            df.loc[ks, "width_u"] = [h.half_width(jc[w][k], l) for k, l in zip(ks, li)]
            # variant: peak lag refined below the 1 ms bin by a parabola through the three
            # bins at the maximum of the smoothed CCG (not the paper's method, which had 0.1 ms bins)
            y0, ym, yp = sm[ks, li], sm[ks, li - 1], sm[ks, li + 1]
            df.loc[ks, "lag_interp"] = lag[ks] + 0.5 * (ym - yp) / (ym - 2 * y0 + yp)
            for nm, arr in [("eff_jc", jc[w]), ("eff_raw", raw), ("eff_sc", sc)]:
                df.loc[ks, nm] = [arr[k, l - 2:l + 3].sum() * 100 for k, l in zip(ks, li)]
            for k in ks:
                sig_ccgs.append((ptype[k], sm[k]))
    pairs.append(df)
    # site averages: V1-V2 pairs grouped by V2 electrode
    v12 = np.where(ptype == "V1V2")[0]
    for e in np.unique(elec[ju][v12]):
        kk = v12[elec[ju][v12] == e]
        row = dict(session=name, animal=name[:3], electrode=int(e), n_pairs=len(kk),
                   n_v2_units=len(np.unique(uidx[ju][kk])), sc=sc[kk].mean(0))
        for w in jc:
            sig, peak, lag, sd = h.significance(h.gauss_smooth(jc[w][kk].mean(0)))
            row[f"sig{w}"] = bool(sig); row[f"peak{w}"] = float(peak); row[f"lag{w}"] = int(lag); row[f"sd{w}"] = float(sd)
        sites.append(row)
    del raw, sc, jc
    div[name] = h.session_divergence(s, seed=1000 + si)
    div[name]["v2_elec"] = s["V2"]["codes"][div[name]["v2_units"], 0]
    del s
    print(f"{name}: {time.time() - t:.0f} s, peak memory {resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / 1e6:.2f} GB")
pairs = pd.concat(pairs, ignore_index=True)
sites = pd.DataFrame(sites)
clock = pd.DataFrame(clock)
print(f"total {time.time() - T0:.0f} s")

Checks of the description against the data:

  • 5 sessions in 3 animals (105, 106, 107), as the descriptor says. Each file holds 6400 rows, alternating a driven trial (1280 ms) and a blank (1500 ms); 400 driven trials per orientation code. Trial ids increase.
  • The descriptor gives an average of 112.2 V1 units per session; the files hold the count printed above. V2: 29.4, as printed.
  • The V2 electrodes are tetrodes, with unit electrode codes 1, 5, 9, ... (the first channel of each tetrode); rfInfo for V2 has one row per channel (28), so a V2 unit's RF is at the row of its electrode code. V1 rfInfo has 96 rows, one per array channel.
  • RF positions and variances are in pixels. Nothing in the data set gives the pixel-to-degree scale or the position of the fixation point, and in four sessions the two eyes' RFs are mapped at the horizontal distances printed above (two gratings, Visual Stimuli). The paper gives 1024 x 768 pixels at 110 cm without the screen size.
  • Clock: orientation is decoded at chance from the end of the preceding blank and in the first 30 ms, and far above chance from 60 ms, with chance accuracy when the labels are shifted by one trial; the V1 population PSTH rises 58 to 68 ms after the start of the driven row, a typical V1 latency. This is consistent with each driven row starting at stimulus onset and with the labels belonging to their own trial.
  • Orientation codes: the sessions description says code 7 is 180 deg in session 105l001p16 (135 deg elsewhere). The population responses to code 7 correlate with those to code 1 (0 deg) more than with codes 6 and 8 in that session only, consistent with that note.
  • No pair of units shares more than half of its spikes at zero lag, apart from those listed above (none listed means no duplicated unit); the five sessions have different unit counts, so no session is deposited twice.
  • Not in the data set: V2 recording depth, penetration identity, unit SNR or waveforms, which the paper's layer groups and single-unit analyses need.

Result: not reproduced. 16 of 31 V2 sites (0.516) have a significant narrow peak in the site-average CCG with the 10 ms jitter, and 22 of 31 (0.710) with the 25 ms variant, against 0.206 +/- 0.021. The fraction is above the paper's in every animal (3 of 6, 5 of 11, 8 of 14) and every session (2 of 5 to 5 of 7), so no single session accounts for it. The data set holds 31 sites against the paper's 223, and the paper says some penetrations targeted middle-layer sites, so the fraction may depend on which sessions were deposited. It may also come from this attempt's method (1 ms bins, no SNR criterion, the jitter implementation); an excess in every session fits either cause, and the data cannot separate them.

Result: not reproduced. 171 of 16,308 V1-V2 pairs (0.0105) have a significant narrow peak with the 10 ms jitter (185, 0.0113, with 25 ms), against 0.003 or 0.00355. The session fractions are 0.0028 to 0.018; only 106r002p70 (0.0028) is within tolerance. Narrow peaks are rare here too, about 1% of pairs. The site fraction (fig4c-narrow-peak-sites) is 2.5 times the paper's, consistent with sessions richer in coupled sites than the paper's sample or with a difference in method (fig4c-narrow-peak-sites).

fig5b-v1v2-latency¶

Narrow V1-V2 CCG peaks are offset from zero lag by a median of 2.8 ms, significantly different from zero, with a mean peak width of 3.71 ms. Expected 2.8 +/- 0.28 ms and 3.71 +/- 0.1 ms; test p < 0.001. At the files' 1 ms resolution the smoothing (Gaussian, SD 1.5 ms) alone gives a single-bin peak a width at half height of 3.54 ms, printed below, so reading (a) cannot fall far below that; the unsmoothed width (reading b) is limited by the 1 ms bin.

Result: not reproduced. Of 171 significant V1-V2 pairs, 151 peak after zero lag and 15 before (sign test p = 1.9e-29, Wilcoxon p = 7.1e-20), so the offset differs from zero with p < 0.001 as the paper reports. The criterion also needs the median offset within 2.8 +/- 0.28 ms, and it is 2.0 ms. The files' 1 ms bins put the peaks at whole milliseconds (55 pairs at 2 ms, 49 at 3 ms); a parabola through the peak bins gives a median of 2.30 ms, also outside. The mean width is 3.89 +/- 0.07 ms on the smoothed CCG and 3.09 ms on the unsmoothed one, both outside 3.71 +/- 0.1; smoothing a single 1 ms bin already gives 3.54 ms.

fig5b-intra-areal-zero-lag¶

Significant narrow peaks of V1-V1 and V2-V2 jitter-corrected CCGs have a median offset of 0.0 ms, not different from zero. Claim of absence; Wilcoxon signed-rank (a) or sign test (b), two-sided, p < 0.05.

The lag sign follows the order of the unit lists (claims file). The data put units of one tetrode, and units of one Utah array channel, together; pairs on the same electrode are shown as a variant without them. The two-sided tests do not depend on which unit of a pair comes first as long as the order is fixed, but a lag asymmetry that follows the order of the unit lists is an ordering effect and not a lead of one population.

In [8]:
for t_ in ["V1V1", "V2V2"]:
    for label, d in [("all pairs", pairs[(pairs.type == t_) & pairs.sig10]),
                     ("different electrodes", pairs[(pairs.type == t_) & pairs.sig10 & (pairs.elec_i != pairs.elec_j)])]:
        l_ = d.lag10.values
        nz = l_[l_ != 0]
        pw = st.wilcoxon(nz).pvalue if len(nz) > 0 else np.nan
        pp = st.wilcoxon(l_, zero_method="pratt").pvalue
        pz = st.wilcoxon(l_, zero_method="zsplit").pvalue
        npos, nneg = (l_ > 0).sum(), (l_ < 0).sum()
        ps = st.binomtest(npos, npos + nneg).pvalue if npos + nneg > 0 else np.nan
        print(f"{t_} {label}: n = {len(l_)} of {(pairs.type == t_).sum()}, median {np.median(l_):.1f} ms, mean {l_.mean():.3f}, "
              f"zero {np.sum(l_ == 0)}, +{npos} / -{nneg}; Wilcoxon p = {pw:.3f} (zeros dropped), {pp:.3f} (Pratt), {pz:.3f} (zeros split); sign test p = {ps:.3f}")

V2V2 all pairs: n = 249 of 2113, median 0.0 ms, mean -0.036, zero 77, +83 / -89; Wilcoxon p = 0.861 (zeros dropped), 0.758 (Pratt), 0.760 (zeros split); sign test p = 0.703
V2V2 different electrodes: n = 108 of 2113, median 0.0 ms, mean -0.148, zero 51, +20 / -37; Wilcoxon p = 0.030 (zeros dropped), 0.024 (Pratt), 0.031 (zeros split); sign test p = 0.033
all offsets plotted lie in -10..10 ms by construction

Result: not reproduced, resting on an assumption. Both medians are 0.0 ms. For the 249 V2-V2 pairs neither test finds a difference from zero (Wilcoxon p = 0.861, sign test p = 0.703). For the 2620 V1-V1 pairs the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, assumed to be the paper's test (see the attempt record), finds one (p = 0.016 with zeros dropped, 0.027 and 0.028 with the other treatments of zeros) and the sign test does not (p = 0.076). The shift is small: mean 0.104 ms, 978 positive and 900 negative offsets, following the order of the unit lists. Without pairs on the same electrode, V2-V2 pairs also differ (108 pairs, Wilcoxon p = 0.030, sign test p = 0.033); the claims file uses all pairs.

The criterion reproduces the claim only when the test finds no difference in both areas and defines no partial outcome. The readings disagree, and the outcome takes the assumed Wilcoxon test (protocol, author step 1.6), under which V1-V1 pairs differ from zero, so the claim is not reproduced. The outcome was partially reproduced after the first two verification rounds, on the ground that the readings disagree; the third round agreed with the change to not reproduced.

figs3-efficacy¶

For significant V1-V2 pairs with peak offsets above 1 ms, the median efficacy (CCG integral within 2.5 ms of the peak) is 0.39%, mean 0.69%. Expected 0.39 +/- 0.039 and 0.69 +/- 0.12.

An offset above 1 ms is, at the files' 1 ms resolution, an offset of 2 ms or more. Efficacy is the sum of the V1-rate-normalised CCG over the five 1 ms bins centred on the peak (-2.5 to +2.5 ms). Readings: (a) the jitter-corrected CCG; (b) the raw CCG, shown both without any correction and shuffle-corrected.

For the 128 significant pairs with offset above 1 ms, the jitter-corrected efficacy (reading a) has median 0.324% and mean 0.496 +/- 0.046%, below 0.39 +/- 0.039 and 0.69 +/- 0.12. On the raw CCG (reading b) the values are far above: median 6.494% uncorrected and 0.820% shuffle-corrected. The median of reading a is 0.334, 0.559 and 0.258% in the three animals.

fig5a-rf-alignment and rf-sizes¶

Blocked, metadata_insufficient: RF centres and variances are in pixels, and the data set gives no pixel-to-degree scale and no fixation point. The paper gives 1024 x 768 pixels at 110 cm without a screen size, so no scale follows from it. For information only, the values in pixels: RF diameter as 4 times the square root of the mean variance (reading a) and the ratio of V2 to V1 diameters, which needs no scale (the paper's values give 2.27 / 1.21 = 1.88); and the probability of a significant pair against the RF offset in pixels, first eye. In sessions with two eyes mapped only the first eye is used. The V1 rfInfo row of a unit is taken as its electrode code minus 1; the cell below checks this against random permutations of the rows.

def rf_of(rf, row):
    return rf[row, :, 0]

for k, v in sess_info.items():
    r1 = v["v1_rf"][:, :, 0]; r2 = v["v2_rf"][:, :, 0]
    ok1 = ~np.isnan(r1[:, 4]) & (r1[:, 4] > 0) & (r1[:, 5] > 0)
    ok2 = ~np.isnan(r2[:, 4]) & (r2[:, 4] > 0) & (r2[:, 5] > 0)
    d1 += list(4 * np.sqrt(r1[ok1, 4:6].mean(1))); d2 += list(4 * np.sqrt(r2[ok2, 4:6].mean(1)))
    d1b += list(4 * (r1[ok1, 4] * r1[ok1, 5]) ** 0.25); d2b += list(4 * (r2[ok2, 4] * r2[ok2, 5]) ** 0.25)

Divergence analyses: groups¶

Middle-layer V2 neurons are the kept V2 units on electrodes whose site-average CCG has a significant narrow peak (fig4c-narrow-peak-sites, 10 ms jitter). The V1 population is every kept V1 unit of the session. Histograms of V1 states from all sessions are put on one support of proportions (k / N1).

Two consequences of the files' 1 ms binning, for all divergence analyses: the V2 spike and the V1 states are both in 1 ms bins, so the epoch of bins 2 and 3 before the spike covers V1 activity from about 1 to 4 ms before it, wider than the paper's 1.5 to 3.5 ms, which may dilute the spike-epoch divergence; and reading e-b (one bin centred 2.5 ms before) cannot be formed, so the single bins 2 ms (e-b2) and 3 ms (e-b3) before stand in for it. The jitter pool includes the spike's own trial (the claims file says other trials), one trial of 400 in the pool.

OFF = list(div[h.SESSIONS[0]]["offsets"])
WIN = h.JITTER_WINDOWS
N_BOOT = 5000

def offset_hist(groupmask, offs, which="raw", w=None, e=0):
    """(neurons, support) histogram pooled over the given offsets, spike (e=0) or control (e=1)."""
    idx = [OFF.index(o) for o in offs]
    if which == "raw":
        hs = [div[k]["raw"][idx, e][:, groupmask[k]].sum(0) for k in h.SESSIONS]
    else:
        hs = [div[k]["jit"][w][idx, e][:, groupmask[k]].sum(0) for k in h.SESSIONS]
    return h.to_global(hs, [div[k]["n_v1"] for k in h.SESSIONS])

def compare(raw_s, jit_s, raw_c, jit_c, rng, per_neuron=False, n_boot=N_BOOT):
    """Spike and control divergence, their bootstrap over neurons and the two p readings."""
    wts = h.boot_weights(raw_s.shape[0], n_boot, rng)
    ds = h.divergence(raw_s, jit_s, per_neuron=per_neuron); dc = h.divergence(raw_c, jit_c, per_neuron=per_neuron)
    bs = h.divergence(raw_s, jit_s, wts, per_neuron); bc = h.divergence(raw_c, jit_c, wts, per_neuron)
    return dict(spike=ds, control=dc, ratio=ds / dc, p_a=h.boot_p_paired(bs, bc), p_b=h.boot_p_indep(bs, bc),
                spike_lo=np.percentile(bs, 2.5), spike_hi=np.percentile(bs, 97.5),
                control_lo=np.percentile(bc, 2.5), control_hi=np.percentile(bc, 97.5), boot_s=bs, boot_c=bc)

def hists_for(groupmask, offs, w, reading):
    """Spike and control histograms (raw and jittered) pooled over the offsets offs, at window w,
    under one reading of the shared method. s-b uses the all-trial pool and control trials,
    r-b the sum of three jitter realizations; the others share the main histograms."""
    if reading in ("main", "d-b", "e-b2", "e-b3"):
        return (offset_hist(groupmask, offs, "raw", e=0), offset_hist(groupmask, offs, "jit", w, e=0),
                offset_hist(groupmask, offs, "raw", e=1), offset_hist(groupmask, offs, "jit", w, e=1))
    ii = [OFF.index(o) for o in offs]
    def hh(e, jit):
        out = []
        for k in h.SESSIONS:
            d = div[k]
            if reading == "s-b":
                x = (d["jit_sb"][w] if jit else d["raw_sb"])[ii, e].sum(0)
            elif jit:   # r-b: mean distribution of three realizations, the main one added
                x = d["jit_rb"][w][ii, e].sum(0) + d["jit"][w][ii, e].sum(0)
            else:
                x = d["raw"][ii, e].sum(0)
            out.append(x[groupmask[k]])
        return h.to_global(out, [div[k]["n_v1"] for k in h.SESSIONS])
    return hh(0, False), hh(0, True), hh(1, False), hh(1, True)

def run_reading(groupmask, rng, before=True, reading="main"):
    """Spike against control divergence at the six windows under one reading of the shared method."""
    rows = []
    sign = 1 if before else -1
    offs = [sign * o for o in {"e-b2": [2], "e-b3": [3]}.get(reading, [2, 3])]
    for w, win in enumerate(WIN):
        rs, js, rc, jcn = hists_for(groupmask, offs, w, reading)
        r = compare(rs, js, rc, jcn, rng, per_neuron=(reading == "d-b"))
        r.update(window=win, reading=reading)
        rows.append(r)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

rng = np.random.default_rng(6)
READINGS = ["main", "e-b2", "e-b3", "s-b", "r-b", "d-b"]
res6a = pd.concat([run_reading(groups, rng, True, r) for r in READINGS], ignore_index=True)

Result: reproduced. The 16 middle-layer sites hold 88 V2 neurons with 1,985,591 spikes from 50 ms. Under the main reading the divergence before V2 spikes is above control at all six windows, 1.72 to 2.43 times, with p < 0.001 under both bootstrap readings (no draw of 5000 under p-a; p-b at most 0.00037). Every other reading (single 1 ms bins 2 or 3 ms before for e-b, s-b, r-b, d-b) also gives 6 of 6 windows. In each animal the ratio is 1.50 or more at every window.

Null check of the bootstrap p-values¶

The two bootstrap readings (p-a paired, p-b independent) are applied to two independent sets of control epochs (same V2 spike times, control trials drawn twice from the same stimulus), where there is no difference to find. Per window at the 1.5 to 3.5 ms epochs before and after (main reading), and for every epoch of the fig7d-time-course scan (2 ms epochs, reading a).

rows = []
for label, offs in [("before", [2, 3]), ("after", [-2, -3])]:
    for w, win in enumerate(WIN):
        r = compare(offset_hist(groups, offs, "raw", e=1), offset_hist(groups, offs, "jit", w, e=1),
                    offset_hist(groups, offs, "raw", e=2), offset_hist(groups, offs, "jit", w, e=2), rng)
        rows.append(dict(epoch=label, window=win, control_1=r["spike"], control_2=r["control"], ratio=r["ratio"], p_a=r["p_a"], p_b=r["p_b"]))
null6 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(null6.to_string(float_format=lambda x: f"{x:.3g}"))
print(f"control against control: p < 0.05 at {(null6.p_a < 0.05).sum()} of {len(null6)} (p-a) and {(null6.p_b < 0.05).sum()} of {len(null6)} (p-b)")
rows = []
for w in range(5):
    for dd in range(-16, 16):
        if abs(dd + 0.5) > 15:
            continue
        offs = [dd, dd + 1]
        r = compare(offset_hist(groups, offs, "raw", e=1), offset_hist(groups, offs, "jit", w, e=1),
                    offset_hist(groups, offs, "raw", e=2), offset_hist(groups, offs, "jit", w, e=2), rng, n_boot=2000)
        rows.append(dict(window=WIN[w], centre=dd + 0.5, diff=r["spike"] - r["control"], p_a=r["p_a"], p_b=r["p_b"]))
nullt = pd.DataFrame(rows)
n_t = len(nullt)
for pr, lab in [("p_a", "p-a"), ("p_b", "p-b")]:
    print(f"time-course scan, control against control, {lab}: p < 0.05 at {(nullt[pr] < 0.05).sum()} of {n_t} epochs "
          f"(expected about {0.05 * n_t:.1f}); Bonferroni-significant (p < 0.05 / 31): {(nullt[pr] < 0.05 / 31).sum()} of {n_t}")
k_a = int((nullt.p_a < 0.05).sum())
print(f"binomial tail, p-a: P(at least {k_a} of {n_t} below 0.05 | rate 0.05) = {st.binom.sf(k_a - 1, n_t, 0.05):.3f} "
      f"(epochs taken as independent, which they are not)")
for w_ in WIN[:5]:
    k_w = int((nullt[nullt.window == w_].p_a < 0.05).sum()); n_w = int((nullt.window == w_).sum())
    print(f"  window {w_} ms: {k_w} of {n_w}, binomial tail P = {st.binom.sf(k_w - 1, n_w, 0.05) if k_w else 1.0:.3f}")
print(nullt.groupby("window").agg(p_a_below_05=("p_a", lambda x: (x < 0.05).sum()), p_b_below_05=("p_b", lambda x: (x < 0.05).sum()),
                                  max_abs_diff=("diff", lambda x: np.abs(x).max())).to_string())

Result: the paired bootstrap (p-a) runs somewhat above its nominal rate at p < 0.05, and the independent one (p-b) is conservative. Comparing two independent control sets, where there is nothing to find, p-a gives p < 0.05 at 1 of 12 window and epoch combinations and at 13 of 150 epochs of the time course scan, against about 7.5 expected (binomial tail P = 0.04 if the epochs were independent, which they are not; 5 of 30 at the 5 ms window). At the Bonferroni threshold it gives 0 of 150. p-b gives p < 0.05 at 0 of 12 and 0 of 150. So single p-a values near 0.05 should be read with care. The largest control-against-control difference in the scan, 4.5e-5 bits at 40 ms and 5.2e-5 at 80 ms, is a scale for the differences found below.

fig7a-threefold¶

For jitter windows of 5 to 80 ms, divergence before middle-layer V2 spikes is roughly 3-fold that of control epochs. Expected ratio 3 +/- 1. Readings (a) geometric mean of the five ratios, (b) median, (c) at least four of five windows within tolerance.

Result: not reproduced. Divergence before V2 spikes is about twice the control divergence, not three times. Under the main reading the ratios at 5 to 80 ms are 1.716 to 2.072, geometric mean 1.906 and median 1.923, below the 2 to 4 tolerance, and 1 of 5 windows is in range. The s-b, r-b and d-b readings give geometric means of 1.837 to 1.903 and medians of 1.836 to 1.927, and 0 or 1 of 5 windows in range. Reading e-b, one bin centred 2.5 ms before, cannot be formed from 1 ms data; the bins 2 and 3 ms before bracket it, with medians of 1.803 and 2.011 and 0 and 3 of 5 windows in range. Only the second, a stand-in for one side of reading e-b, reaches the edge of the tolerance, under the median summary alone.

fig7a-above-shuffle¶

Divergence both before middle-layer V2 spikes and in control epochs is significantly larger than divergence of shuffled data. Readings: trials permuted within orientation (a) or across all trials (b); epochs of the shuffled data spike-triggered (c) or control (d). Reproduced when the lower 95% bootstrap bound of both spike and control divergence is above the shuffled value at every window from 5 to 80 ms.

The margin is thin at 5 ms with trials shuffled within orientation: over five shuffle realizations the shuffled value there has mean 1.935e-4 (spike epochs) and 1.928e-4 (control epochs), SD about 1e-5, against a control bound of 2.013e-4, and one realization of five in each of these two readings is above the bound (2.073e-4 and 2.038e-4), leaving 4 of 5 windows. At every other window and reading all five realizations are below both bounds.

Result: not reproduced. After V2 spikes the divergence is above control at 80 ms under both bootstrap readings and every reading of the method (main: ratio 1.37, no draw of 5000 under p-a, p-b = 0.0038; p-b 0.046 or less in the others), and at 40 ms under p-a (main ratio 1.20). Under the main reading the ratios at 5 to 20 ms are 1.03 to 1.08 (p-a 0.10 to 0.48); in other readings they range from 0.959 (s-b, 10 ms) to 1.12 (d-b, 20 ms, p-a = 0.024). The elevation after the spike is smaller than before it (main, at 40 and 80 ms, 1.20 and 1.37 after against 1.96 and 2.07 before). The main after-spike differences at 40 and 80 ms (1.2e-4 and 2.7e-4 bits) are well above the largest difference between two control sets in the null check (4.5e-5 and 5.2e-5), so they are not an artefact of the test; p-b alone decides the outcome at 80 ms.

At a jitter window of 1280 ms, V1 divergence is elevated both before and after middle-layer V2 spikes.

fig7d-time-course¶

Enhanced V1 coordination is evident several milliseconds before middle-layer V2 spikes, but not in more distant epochs or after V2 spikes.

Difference in divergence (spike minus control) at offsets within 15 ms, windows 5 to 80 ms, under the main reading and the s-b, r-b and d-b readings of the shared method (e-b is the single-bin reading b below). Offsets: (a) 2 ms epochs stepped by 1 ms (centre d + 0.5 for bins d and d + 1); (b) single 1 ms bins (centre d). Positive centres are before the spike. An epoch counts as after the spike when it lies wholly after it (centre -1 or less); the epochs holding the simultaneous bin (centre -0.5 in a, 0 in b) are counted apart as sig_at_spike. Bootstrap p under both readings p-a and p-b, Bonferroni over the offsets of a window (31). 2000 draws per comparison: the smallest p it can give, 1/2000, is below the corrected threshold 0.05/31 = 0.0016, and 5000 draws for 1240 comparisons per method would not fit the notebook's time.

In [19]:
def time_course(groupmask, rng, method="main", n_boot=2000):
    rows = []
    for rd in ["a", "b"]:
        epochs_ = [([d, d + 1], d + 0.5) for d in range(-16, 16) if abs(d + 0.5) <= 15] if rd == "a" else [([d], float(d)) for d in range(-15, 16)]
        for w in range(5):
            for offs, c in epochs_:
                rs, js, rc, jcn = hists_for(groupmask, offs, w, method)
                r = compare(rs, js, rc, jcn, rng, per_neuron=(method == "d-b"), n_boot=n_boot)
                rows.append(dict(method=method, reading=rd, window=WIN[w], centre=c, diff=r["spike"] - r["control"], p=r["p_a"],
                                 p_b=r["p_b"], n_off=len(epochs_)))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

rng = np.random.default_rng(74)
tc_all = pd.concat([time_course(groups, rng, m) for m in ["main", "s-b", "r-b", "d-b"]], ignore_index=True)
tc = tc_all[tc_all.method == "main"].copy()
def judge_tc(tc):
    """After the spike: epochs wholly after it (centre -1 or less); the epochs holding the
    simultaneous bin (centre -0.5 in reading a, 0 in reading b) are counted apart."""
    out = []
    for (rd, win), d in tc.groupby(["reading", "window"]):
        best = d.loc[d["diff"].idxmax()]
        bad = d[d.sig_up & ((d.centre <= -1) | (d.centre > 8))]
        at0 = d[d.sig_up & d.centre.isin([-0.5, 0.0])]
        out.append(dict(reading=rd, window=win, peak_centre=best.centre, peak_diff=best["diff"],
                        peak_in_1_6=1 <= best.centre <= 6, sig_before_1_6=int((d.sig_up & d.centre.between(1, 6)).sum()),
                        sig_at_spike=len(at0), sig_after_or_far=len(bad), bad_centres=list(bad.centre)))
    return pd.DataFrame(out)
for m in ["main", "s-b", "r-b", "d-b"]:
    for pr in ["p", "p_b"]:
        t_ = tc_all[tc_all.method == m].copy()
        t_["sig_up"] = (t_[pr] < 0.05 / t_.n_off) & (t_["diff"] > 0)
        jt = judge_tc(t_)
        print(f"method {m}, bootstrap p reading {'p-a' if pr == 'p' else 'p-b'}: peak 1 to 6 ms before at {jt.peak_in_1_6.sum()} of 10 "
              f"(reading, window) cells; windows with a significant epoch after or far, reading a: {(jt[jt.reading == 'a'].sig_after_or_far > 0).sum()} of 5, "
              f"reading b: {(jt[jt.reading == 'b'].sig_after_or_far > 0).sum()} of 5")
        if m == "main" or pr == "p_b":
            print(jt.to_string(float_format=lambda x: f"{x:.3g}"))
print(tc.pivot_table(index="centre", columns=["reading", "window"], values="diff").loc[lambda x: x.index.isin([-10, -5, -2.5, -2, 0, 0.5, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 5, 10])].to_string(float_format=lambda x: f"{x:.1e}"))

ax[0].set_ylabel("spike - control (bits)")

Result: partially reproduced. Under every reading of the method (main, s-b, r-b, d-b) and both offset readings, the largest difference at each of the five windows is 2.5 to 3.5 ms before the V2 spike (main: 2.5 ms for 2 ms epochs, 3 ms for 1 ms bins). Some epochs wholly after the spike or more than 8 ms before it are also above control after the Bonferroni correction. With the paired bootstrap (p-a), which the null check finds somewhat above its nominal rate at p < 0.05 but with no Bonferroni-significant epoch, this holds at every window in every reading (main, reading a: 10 to 19 epochs per window). With the independent bootstrap (p-b) it holds at 80 ms in the main, s-b and r-b readings (4 to 6 epochs, for example main reading a: 1.5, 6.5, 7.5, 8.5 and 9.5 ms after), and at 40 and 80 ms in d-b. These differences are smaller than near the spike: at 80 ms, 2.7e-4 bits for the epoch 2.5 ms after against 8.3e-4 for the epoch 2.5 ms before.

Result: reproduced. 39 middle-layer neurons have a significant pair with a V1 unit and 49 have none. Under the main reading both subsets have spike divergence above control at all five windows under p-a, and under p-b at 5 of 5 with a partner and 4 of 5 without (at 5 ms p = 0.150). Across the six readings, the subset with a partner is above control at 5 of 5 windows under both p readings, and the subset without at 4 or 5 of 5 under p-a and 2 to 5 of 5 under p-b. One combination does not meet the criterion: under e-b2 (the single bin 2 ms before, a stand-in for one side of reading e-b) with p-b, the subset without a partner is above control at 2 of 5 windows. The outcome holds under the other readings, as the criterion takes any reading. The ratio is larger with a partner at all five windows in every reading (main 1.91 to 2.30 against 1.32 to 1.67).

  • fig4-narrow-peak-depth, fig7b-nonmiddle-no-coordination, fig7e-nonmiddle-time-course, figs5-middle-layer-relay: need V2 depth or the order of sites in a penetration; the files hold one recording per V2 electrode per session and no depth (data_missing).
  • fig7c-offset-rf-no-coordination: needs depth (500 to 1000 um from the layer 6/WM border) and RF offsets in degrees (data_missing).
  • figs2a-v2-single-units, figs2b-v1-single-units: need unit SNR; the files hold no waveforms or SNR (data_missing).
  • fig5a-rf-alignment, rf-sizes: need RF positions in degrees (metadata_insufficient).
  • fig1-ffn-propagation, fig3-divergence-correlation, figs1-higher-order, fig8-architecture: simulations with no published code (data: elsewhere); nothing stops a rerun from the Supplemental Experimental Procedures, but it was not attempted here (other).

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's:

  • Spike times are at 1 ms in the files; the paper's CCGs used 0.1 ms bins. Peak offsets are whole milliseconds here, the smoothing alone gives a peak 3.54 ms wide, and the 1.5 to 3.5 ms epoch covers about 1 to 4 ms.
  • Units are kept by rate only; the SNR criterion cannot be applied.
  • Sites are V2 electrodes in a session, 31 in all against 223; depth, penetration and layer are not known, so the non-middle-layer and offset-RF groups cannot be formed.
  • Readings of open details follow the claims file: the CCG jitter window (10 ms; 25 ms as a variant), the epoch (two 1 ms bins; e-b approximated by one bin at 2 or 3 ms), the stratum of the jitter and control trials, one or three jitter realizations, pooled or per-neuron distributions, and paired or independent bootstrap p-values. A null check (control against control) finds the paired bootstrap somewhat above its nominal rate at p < 0.05 (13 of 150 epochs, about 7.5 expected; none at the Bonferroni threshold) and the independent one conservative.

What was found about the data set:

  • It holds 5 sessions from 3 animals, with 564 V1 and 147 V2 units; the descriptor's mean of 112.2 V1 units per session does not match the 112.8 in the files.
  • No V2 depth, penetration identity, unit SNR or waveforms; the paper's laminar and single-unit analyses cannot be repeated.
  • RF positions and sizes are in pixels with no scale or fixation point; the paper does not give the screen size either.
  • Narrow V1-V2 peaks are found at about half of the sites, against a fifth in the paper. The difference may come from which sessions were deposited, a selection the documentation does not describe, or from this attempt's method (1 ms bins, no SNR criterion, the jitter implementation); the data cannot separate the two.
  • The descriptor's list of orientation codes does not hold for session 105l001p16, where code 7 is 180 deg (sessions description); the population responses agree with the latter.
